description: Prompts for preparing for property tax conversations with your accountant or registered tax agent.

cards.title: Accountant Prep Pack
cards.description: Walk into your tax agent appointment with the right questions already written.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian property tax preparation assistant. I want to prepare for a conversation with my accountant about the tax implications of an investment property.

PROPERTY: [suburb, state, type, year built, $price]
PURPOSE: [investment — rental]
OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE (considering): [personal / joint / trust / SMSF / unsure]
MY TAX RATE: approximately [32.5% / 37% / 45%]
INCOME TYPE: [PAYG / self-employed]
OTHER PROPERTIES: [none / describe]

Please return:
1. Tax-relevant property facts summary
2. Likely deductible expenses list (flag each as 'verify with tax agent')
3. Common non-deductible items to discuss
4. 10 specific questions for my accountant (negative gearing, depreciation, CGT, ownership, land tax)
5. Document checklist for the accountant meeting

DISCLAIMER: General information and preparation only — not tax advice. Tax treatment depends on individual circumstances. Seek advice from a registered tax agent.
cards.best_for: Investors preparing for their first accountant conversation about a new investment property
cards.professional_review_note: This pack is preparation only. A registered tax agent gives the actual tax advice.

cards.title: Capital Gains Tax Planning Questions
cards.description: Prepare questions about CGT before speaking to your accountant — especially relevant given proposed 2027 changes.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian property tax preparation assistant. I want to prepare questions about capital gains tax before meeting my accountant.

MY SITUATION: I own [describe property/properties, purchase dates, and purpose: investment / PPOR]
MY CONCERN: [e.g. timing a sale / the proposed 1 July 2027 CGT changes / general CGT planning]

Please help me understand and prepare questions about:
1. How CGT is calculated on investment property (cost base, discount, indexation)
2. The 50% CGT discount — when it applies and the holding period requirement
3. The proposed CGT changes (if any are relevant to my situation) — current status
4. Main residence exemption — when and how it applies
5. 6 specific questions to ask my accountant about my specific CGT position

IMPORTANT: Flag clearly that proposed CGT changes are not yet law and status must be verified.

DISCLAIMER: General information and preparation only — not tax advice. CGT is complex and individual-specific. Seek advice from a registered tax agent.
cards.best_for: Investors thinking about timing a sale or wanting to understand the CGT implications of their portfolio
cards.output_type: CGT planning education and question list
cards.professional_review_note: CGT calculations and planning must be done by a registered tax agent. Proposed law changes require confirmation of current status.
